A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same lower-bound study. Their main text, equations, Figure 1, references, and complete appendix proofs are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports theoretical constructions, lower bounds, and proofs, including in its appendices. Figure 1 is a schematic; no original experimental, simulation, or data-analysis outcomes are reported.

after.justification: v3 remains entirely theoretical throughout the main text and appendices. It reports no original empirical outcomes.

M1.justification: The deterministic and stochastic hard-instance constructions and zero-chain mechanism are retained: v1 Equations (6) and (14) correspond to v3 Equations (5) and (10). No optimization algorithm or model component is introduced or substantively revised.

E1.justification: Neither version trains or evaluates on datasets or application tasks. The added discussion of finite-sum problems concerns prior theoretical work, not newly evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: Neither version experimentally evaluates comparison methods. The added references and complexity-bound comparisons change research positioning, not an evaluated baseline set.

E3.justification: Neither version contains experimental splits, training budgets, evaluation metrics, or testing procedures. The theoretical stationarity criteria and stochastic-oracle setup are retained.

E4.justification: No ablations, robustness experiments, error analyses, or empirical case studies occur in either version. The stochastic analysis moved into v3's appendix already appeared in v1 Section 5.3.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental runs, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The oracle variance assumptions, Bernoulli construction, and probability bounds are unchanged theoretical content.

E6.justification: Neither version contains empirical result entries. The paper's original deterministic and stochastic lower-bound rates, Ω(κ^(3/2) ε^-2) and Ω(κ^(5/2) ε^-4), and their associated hardness findings remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v3 corrects Definition 4 so the lower-level oracle returns g rather than f, and Section 5.2 removes the intermediate O(||F(x)||_2) equality from the mixed-derivative calculation. The principal theorems, constructions, and appendix proofs otherwise retain their mathematical content.

C1.justification: The abstract's bounds and main hardness claims are unchanged. Section 5.2 narrows the novelty wording: v1 claims the first lower bound for stochastic bilevel optimization, whereas v3 claims the first such result demonstrating greater hardness than both single-level and min-max optimization.

C2.justification: Section 3.1 changes the unconditional statement that smoothness constants are independent of μ and ε into a description of the regime of primary interest. Section 5.2 qualifies matching Kwon et al.'s conditions as approximate. Existing complexity gaps and future-work limitations are retained after relocation.

D1.justification: Neither version supplies experimental implementation details, hardware, training times, or code/data access instructions. The construction parameters and technical proof specifications are retained, including material moved to the appendix.

R1.justification: v3 adds discussion of Dagréou et al. (2024), comparison with Zhang et al. (2021), and a paragraph distinguishing concurrent Chen and Zhang (2025). It also corrects the introductory Li et al. bound from Ω(κ ε^-2) to Ω(sqrt(κ) ε^-2), matching the value already stated in v1 Section 4.2. These are focused additions within the retained research positioning.

P1.justification: The document is substantially reorganized: v1 Section 5.3 moves to an appendix, the future-work discussion leaves the conclusion for another appendix, and references move before the appendices. v3 also adds impact and acknowledgment sections and edits introductory prose. The reorganization introduces duplicate appendix labels A and B.

P2.justification: The single-column manuscript becomes a conference-style document with two-column main text and references, full-width appendices, new headers, and extensively reformatted equation displays. Figure 1 retains its content but is resized and relocated from before the deterministic theorem to after the construction. No tables or new figures are added.

improvement.justification: v3 improves scholarly accuracy through the added finite-sum and concurrent-work comparisons, narrower novelty wording, and corrections to the introductory deterministic comparison and oracle definition. The central results and proofs remain unchanged. Duplicate appendix labels A and B introduce a navigation defect, but the substantive clarification and accuracy gains support a limited overall improvement.
